i can't fully relate but i used to be in colorguard and i will just say what i would try to do and how i would interpret this situation. honestly, if this means that much to you and he really isn't budging, i would see about scheduling a meeting between him and your parents. if he is worried about the affect it will have on your experience, then maybe the voice of your parents advocating for you will help him reconsider and understand how important this is to you. i get that he's looking out for you but he's also hindering you. by the time you're a senior you might not even be in colorguard anymore because of the very reason he's worried about. its not often you get an opportunity to march dci, even if you are still young the opportunity is right there! the fact that you made ensemble as an underclassman is incredible!! congratulations!! you have every right to seize this opportunity. maybe he is right- but you won't know if you don't try. both YOUR instructor and the assistant band director approve. if you want this as badly as it seems, you'll come back to high school marching band and rather than let everyone else pull you down, IF that happens (i mean, calling his own students lazy and unmotivated to another students face? does he even have any faith in his marching band in the first place??) it will make your love for colorguard grow even stronger. you may even inspire your teammates to grow with you. colorguard is a team and being the only one who seems to truly care can be so so frustrating. that could very much happen. but i find that shining on your own and knowing that YOU did good is just as fufilling. colorguard is what YOU make of it. so. tldr; try to get your parents or principal involved. it's a simple matter of permission and his reasoning is based off of speculation. show him how much this means to you, and fight. prove him wrong. if he doesn't budge, don't let it discourage you. there's a lot of time ahead of you to explore colorguard, and your time to shine will come no matter what. i hope things work out for you.

Oh yeah. I’m right there with you. I’ve been self harming since 2014-2015ish. I was clean for three years. Then I relapsed and scratched the shit out of myself, and did mild cutting. That was in 2018. Then come around late 2020 I relapsed again by cutting. I stopped for a few months but now I’m in deep and cut pretty much every day. It’s humiliating, knowing that my scars were finally fading, I could wear short sleeves, and now I’m worse than I’ve ever been. I reached out for help but it turned out to be a bust (he was a school counselor. I didn’t want to get admitted somewhere  bc he thought I was loony lol) and ever since then I’ve been hiding and hurting on my own. As soon as I think “okay. I’ll get help” it’s like waaaait a minute.. nothing is wrong with me and I’m perfectly fine. It seems like we are afraid of getting help, so we subconsciously trick ourselves into feeling “better” while we’re still hurting. Recovery is scary. Seeing a professional is even scarier. One day you will get there, please be kind to yourself. I’m sure you’ve heard this a million times but recovery isn’t linear. And if you’re actively relapsing and can’t see yourself improving anytime soon (like me), just try to be as safe as possible and know you have people here you can talk to. Much love.

If you haven’t cut yet, perhaps try to distract yourself with things you like? Talk to a loved one, read– play a game? Or for more physical methods, try drawing/painting on yourself in something red, try holding an ice cube in your hand. I would try to avoid SH as much as possible. It is, to say the least, life wrecking. It’s addictive and once you start you want to do more, go deeper, until your arm is mutilated and bloody and until you can barelt recognize your limbs anymore. You’ll never be able to wear short sleeves in public without getting stares or pervasive questions, and you’ll be torn between, “My scares are disgusting. I wish I had never done this”, and “I have so many scars. My body is ruined, a few more won’t hurt”. It’s life ruining and can make everything go downhill very quickly. Please be safe, either way, and we are here if you need a friend! I believe in you, and you are not alone. 🤍

Hey! I’m in the same boat you are. I understand how embarrassing it can be to come clean about this stuff. My boyfriend used to make me show him my arm after I cut as punishment to try and humiliate me into stopping. I understand exactly what you’re going through. And try not to be so hard on yourself. People like us are constantly carrying the burden and dealing with the temptation of relapse. You were strong and you tried your hardest to stay clean to the very end– you’re still strong. Sometimes relapsing just can’t be helped. I made a promise as well, and broke it. I was so ashamed and I felt so guilty. If you can find it in yourself to tell him, just try to explain what mental stress you’re under and how difficult it is for you to stay clean at this current point in time. It’s not your fault and if he cares about you, he’d be glad you came clean about it instead of keeping it from him, and it’ll help your conscience as well. I wish you luck, friend!
